findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget path renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true the component renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. Because `columns` is an empty array (not nullish), `TableWidgetVisualization`'s fallback to derive columns from `tableData.meta.fields` is also bypassed. The consequence is that every table widget on a dashboard renders completely blank (no headers, no rows) for any organization that has this flag enabled, silently hiding real widget data. Either wire the real data through or keep the new component behind code that is not reachable from a user-facing flag.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes nodestore preserves input ordering
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a dict keyed by node id), and then pairs them positionally with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This relies on the backend returning values in exactly the same order as the requested ids and on never omitting missing keys. Some backends (e.g. Bigtable, which returns rows sorted by row key) do not guarantee that, and any omitted/missing entry shifts the pairing. The result is `ErrorEvent.id` being attached to the wrong error's title/message/timestamp, so the summary sent to Seer references incorrect event ids. Iterate `node_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)` per id instead.

findings.title: Error/breadcrumb merge compares timestamps in different units
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors and replay events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from the nodestore event payload and are epoch *seconds* (e.g. 1718900000.0), while rrweb replay event `timestamp` values are epoch *milliseconds* (e.g. 1718900000000). With real data every error timestamp is ~1000x smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp, so all errors are emitted before all breadcrumbs regardless of when they actually occurred, defeating the purpose of the chronological merge (and the log text prints raw, mismatched numbers). Normalise both to the same unit before comparing. The new unit test passes only because it uses hand-written second-scale event timestamps.

findings.title: React Query key no longer includes the organization
findings.body: The hook was switched from `useApiQuery([path, options])` (where `path` contained `/organizations/${organization.slug}/...`) to `useQuery({queryKey: ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]})`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` only contains itemType, attributeType, project ids and the datetime range. When the project selection is "all projects" (`projects: []`), two different organizations produce an identical cache key, so attribute keys fetched for one org can be served from cache to another org. Add the organization slug (and ideally the endpoint path) to the query key.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline is likely too short for a 100-identity chunk
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` is scheduled by `check_auth` with `chunk_size=100` and sequentially calls `check_single_auth_identity` for each id; each call does a DB read, an RPC membership check and `provider.refresh_identity()`, which performs an external IdP request. A 60s `processing_deadline_duration` gives ~0.6s per identity. If the deadline is hit, the task is killed mid-chunk and (a) the remaining identities were already stamped with `last_synced=now` in `check_auth`, so they will not be re-selected for roughly another AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL, and (b) the trailing `check_auth.apply_async(...)` that chains the next chunk never runs, stalling the whole sweep. Either raise the deadline substantially or reduce the chunk size.

findings.title: Both saved-search conversion migrations turned into no-ops pointing at a migration not in this change
findings.body: `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised` both have their `RunPython` bodies replaced with `return` and a comment saying "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration". No such migration is added in this PR, and the only test covering the conversion (`tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py`) is deleted. If 0921 does not exist, organization-visibility `SavedSearch` rows are never converted into `GroupSearchView` rows anywhere, and the codebase is left with two dead migrations whose comments reference a nonexistent file plus zero test coverage for the conversion logic.

findings.title: One invalid report rejects the entire browser report batch
findings.body: The loop validates each report and returns `422` for the whole request as soon as any single report fails validation, so all other valid reports in the same batch are dropped. Browsers send Reporting API payloads as batches and will retry the whole batch, meaning a single persistently malformed/unsupported report (e.g. a `type` not in `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES`, or a `url` the `URLField` regex rejects) permanently blocks metrics for every other report delivered with it. Prefer skipping/counting the invalid entries (with a metric or log) and returning 200 for the rest.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness instead of presence
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Since both use truthiness, a value of `0` counts as absent: a report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators even though the stated rule is that exactly one of the two fields may be present, and a report with `timestamp: <valid>` plus `age: 0` produces an error only on the `age` field. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` instead.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a per-issue recommended-event lookup while building PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper runs a search/Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per group, so building one comment now performs up to 5 extra event lookups (per PR, for both GitHub and GitLab comment workflows) purely to render an environment name. Consider resolving environments with a single cheap query (e.g. GroupEnvironment) instead of fetching recommended events, and note that the broad `except Exception` silently degrades to no environment on any failure.

findings.title: Issue titles are interpolated into a markdown link without escaping
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* \u203c\ufe0f [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` now puts the (truncated) issue title inside markdown link text, whereas the previous template only bolded it. Issue titles frequently contain `[` / `]` (e.g. `KeyError: 'items[0]'`), which terminates the link text early and renders a broken link/raw brackets in the PR comment. Escape `[`, `]` (and backslashes) in the title before formatting.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature check and request validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is the first statement in `post()`, so it fires even when the organization lacks `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` (404 response) or when the body fails schema validation (400 response). The resulting metric therefore counts rejected calls as assemble attempts. Move the `analytics.record` call after the feature/validation gates (or after the task is queued) so it reflects actual assembles.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers returning falsy React nodes are silently overridden
findings.body: Both `renderDefaultHeadCell` and `renderDefaultBodyCell` do `const cell = render...(...); if (cell) return cell;`. The documented contract (see tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx and the prop JSDoc) is that only `undefined` falls through to the default renderer, but `null`, `''` and `0` are valid React nodes meaning "render this" and will instead be replaced by the default rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` so a custom renderer can intentionally render nothing.

findings.title: Dead _handle_regex_match helper left in parametrize_w_experiments
findings.body: After removing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment`, the experiment loop always calls `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`, but the inner `_handle_regex_match` closure (lines 335-343) is still defined and is now unreachable dead code duplicating the helper in `parametrize_w_regex`. Remove it to avoid confusion about which callback experiments use.
